alignments.note: Temporal conjunction realized by the word introducing its English clause (rule 40).
Substantival article rendered *that which*; head on the nominal *that* rather than the relativizer (rules 22, 77).
Adjectival predicate takes the supplied copula (rule 53); head on the adjective.
Aorist subjunctive rendered by the English perfect *is come*; head on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17).
Substantival article rendered *that which*; head on *that* (rules 22, 77).
Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause carries the supplied copula (rule 53); head on the prepositional word.
Future passive with its auxiliaries; head on the lexical verb word *done* (rules 9, 17).

review_notes: Both substantival articles take *that which* whole and head on *that*, no participle following to carry the relativizer (rules 22, 32, 77).

The copula of the second clause goes to the preposition rather than to the article, the prepositional phrase being the predicate (rule 53); in the first clause the adjective takes it on the same reasoning.
